Resumption is refused if the halt was triggered by a mid-write exhaustion (the reservation check failed or was absent) or if tail integrity validation fails.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The reservation check uses an estimated token cost that can be exceeded by actual write cost (estimate error).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The hash chain uses a weak algorithm vulnerable to collision during the pause window.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The integrity check validates structure but not semantic consistency (events are well-formed but causally disconnected).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The reservation check was present but the system also performed non-event writes (e.g., temporary files) that were interrupted.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A pre-write reservation check creates a causal guarantee: the system never enters a state where an event write is in progress at exhaustion. This makes every halt point a safe resumption boundary by construction. Tail integrity validation on resumption detects any corruption that occurred during the pause (storage decay, external mutation). Together, these two mechanisms form a sufficient condition: the former guarantees no partial writes at halt, the latter detects post-halt corruption. Without either, the guarantee collapses.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
